rationale.intervention_reconstruction: The hypothesis proposes adding yttrium to form oxide dispersoids, whereas the paper varied vanadium content in W–Ta alloys to exploit chemical short-range order and defect mobility changes. This is a different kind of intervention (oxide-dispersion strengthening vs. solid-solution alloying with V).
rationale.condition_agreement: The hypothesis mentions 500–1000 °C under fusion-relevant irradiation, while the paper used 1073 K (800 °C) with 1 MeV Kr ions. The temperature range overlaps but the hypothesis lacks the specific deposition, annealing, and ion-beam conditions of the paper.
rationale.mechanism_agreement: The hypothesis invokes defect trapping at oxide particles, whereas the paper's mechanism relies on V-induced changes in self-interstitial mobility, defect recombination, and suppression of chemical short-range order and segregation. These are different classes of mechanism.
rationale.outcome_agreement: The hypothesis predicts reduced swelling and maintained strength, while the paper measured void size/density, grain stability, and segregation. The general direction (improved radiation tolerance) aligns, but the specific property and metrics differ.
